Build a NEW marketing homepage concept for Nxeon at route `/newwebsitev6`. This is one of four concepts being built in parallel for a bake-off; yours must be visually unmistakable from the others.

## Your concept: v6 — "Editorial". LIGHT MODE, print-inspired.

This is the only light-mode concept of the four, so commit to it fully — a confident, bright, paper-like page. Think a design annual, a well-set architecture monograph, or a premium print magazine that happens to be about infrastructure. Generous measure, strong typographic hierarchy, large photographic key art used sparingly and at real scale.

**Critical:** do NOT produce the warm-cream-plus-serif-plus-terracotta look (#F4F1EA grounds, terracotta/rust accents, broadsheet hairline rules). That exact palette is the single most recognisable AI-generated-design cliché and the owner has explicitly rejected AI-looking work. Pick a *cool* paper white or a tinted neutral, and an accent that isn't terracotta/rust/burnt-orange.

- Ground: a chosen off-white with a slight hue bias — not pure #fff, not warm cream. Deep ink for text, not pure black.
- Type: a characterful display face — a real serif or a high-contrast display — paired with a clean text face. NOT Inter, Geist, or Space Grotesk. Load via `next/font/google`.
- Use the game key art and portal art as full-bleed or large editorial images; light mode gives you the contrast to make dark imagery sing.
- Interaction: editorial-appropriate — a hover-revealed detail layer, an index that tracks scroll position, figure captions that expand. Tactile, not flashy.

The audience is founders and small businesses — people who want to look credible and don't care about kernel flags.

## Repo context

- Root: `/opt/nxeon`. Next.js App Router, Tailwind v4, TypeScript. **Work directly in /opt/nxeon.**
- Create `app/newwebsitev6/layout.tsx`, `app/newwebsitev6/page.tsx`, `app/newwebsitev6/v6.css`, plus client components in that directory. **Touch no files outside `app/newwebsitev6/`** — three other agents are working in this same checkout in parallel.
- The layout must wrap children in `<div className="v6 ...">` and scope ALL your CSS under `.v6`. Import your css from the layout.
- Set `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` in the layout's `metadata`.
- **Light mode specifically:** the root layout's `globals.css` is a dark-first design system. Your `.v6` wrapper must set its own `background` and `color` explicitly and not rely on inherited tokens. Watch for Tailwind utilities that fight you (e.g. `text-slate-200`) — prefer your own scoped tokens.
- Page should be a Server Component (`export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`).

## Real data sources (use these — do not hardcode numbers)

- `db.plan` — VPS plans (`priceCents`, `active`). Cheapest active ~$8.99.
- `db.gamePlan` — game plans: `gameFamily`, `ramMB`, `slots`, `priceCents`, `active`. 42 active families.
- `db.gameMod.count({ where: { active: true, upstreamOk: true } })` — mod catalogue size.
- `db.osTemplate` — real one-click templates (`name`, `active`).
- Regions: `regionsFrom` from `@/lib/nx/catalog` with `db.node.findMany({ where: { enabled: true }, select: { id: true, region: true } })` → exactly TWO: Singapore and Germany. `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS` from `@/lib/node-regions`.
- Game metadata: `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG`, `GAME_GENRES` from `@/lib/games`; `GAME_URL_SLUG` from `@/lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings`.
- `db` is `import { db } from "@/lib/db"`.

## HONESTY CONSTRAINTS — hard requirements

- **No testimonials, reviews, or ratings.** `Review` and `Testimonial` tables are empty. Do not invent any. No Google/Trustpilot widgets.
- **No invented statistics.** No customer counts, no data-centre counts, no continents. Exactly TWO regions.
- **No partner or customer logos** implying a relationship. Real one-click templates are fine. Third-party tool logos must be framed "works with", no affiliation implied.
- Pre-approved claims you MAY use: `99.99% network`, and the tagline `online in 47 seconds`.
- Prices must come from the database.

## Known traps in this codebase

- **Do NOT export an object-of-components from a `"use client"` module and read properties off it in a Server Component** (`export const Icon = {...}` then `<Icon.x/>` in the server page) — resolves to `undefined` and React throws "Element type is invalid". Put shared SVG icons in a module with NO `"use client"`.
- `.v6 .card { position: relative }` (specificity 0,2,0) **beats** Tailwind's `lg:absolute` (0,1,0). Put positioning utilities on a wrapper if they must win.
- `public/logos/caddy.svg` is a 0-byte file — don't reference it.
- Grids stretch rows to the tallest sibling; use `content-start`/`items-start` to avoid dead bands.
- Keep the page readable **at rest** — never park content at `opacity: 0` waiting on a scroll observer. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Assets

- `/logo.png` and `/nx-mark.png` — the real brand marks (a blue→violet NX monogram). **On a light ground, check they still read.** If the mark doesn't work on your background, note it in your report rather than recolouring the brand yourself.
- `public/games/art/<slug>_poster.jpg` and `_hero.jpg` — real game key art (3:4 posters and 16:9 heroes).
- `public/nx/art/*.webp` — portal illustration art (`activity-hero`, `billing-hero`, `database`, `gamepad`, `globe-network`, `partner-hero`).
- `public/logos/*.svg` — real app/OS logos.

## Process

Two-pass design process: write a short design plan first (palette as 4-6 named hex values, 2+ typefaces with roles, layout concept), then **review it against the concept** and revise anything that reads like the generic default, noting what you changed. Then write code.

Build the hero plus 3-4 sections. Fewer, better sections.

## Rules

- `npx tsc --noEmit` from `/opt/nxeon` must pass when you're done. Other agents are editing the same checkout, so errors under `app/newwebsitev5|v7|v8/**` are not yours — ignore them and confirm your own files are clean.
- **Do NOT run any git command. Do NOT commit, branch, or stage anything.** Leave your files on disk; the parent session commits all four concepts together.
- **Do NOT deploy and do NOT run `npm run build`.**
- Report back: what you built (file list), your design plan and what self-review changed, and anything you couldn't verify.

/**
 * VPS INTRO PRICING — a LOW first-term price that RENEWS at the regular price
 * (classic hosting promo: "$3.99/mo first term, renews at $6.49/mo").
 *
 * This is deliberately modelled as a FIRST-TERM-ONLY discount so it rides the
 * plumbing the platform already has, rather than adding a second renewal price:
 *
 *   - The ORDER (lib/order.ts) charges the intro-reduced first term and stamps the
 *     implied first-term rate on `Server.termPromoPercent` (the very column every
 *     later proration/refund already prices against — see lib/proration.ts).
 *   - RENEWAL (lib/renewal-charge.ts — the SINGLE renewal formula) reads
 *     `plan.priceCents` and knows NOTHING about `introPriceCents`, so a renewal is
 *     billed at the regular price by construction. No renewal code changes.
 *
 * Pure & deterministic (no `db`, no I/O), so it can be imported by the order core,
 * the marketing pricing cards and unit tests alike. The two READERS below cast to
 * reach `introPriceCents` / `introTermMonths` because the symlinked prod Prisma
 * client's types predate these columns until it is regenerated at deploy — the
 * same stale-client gap `frozenProductAnnualPct` (lib/product-billing.ts) and the
 * `Server` writes in lib/order.ts already work around. Identical at runtime once
 * the client is regenerated.
 */
import { termDiscountPct } from "./billing-terms";

/** A row that MAY carry the intro columns (present at runtime, absent from stale types). */
type PlanIntroFields = { introPriceCents?: number | null; introTermMonths?: number | null };

/**
 * The plan's intro MONTHLY price in cents, or null when it is unset, malformed, or
 * NOT genuinely below the regular price. Requiring `intro < regular` means a bad /
 * equal / higher value can never quietly RAISE the first-term charge — it just
 * disables the intro and the plan bills its regular price.
 *
 * `plan` is typed loose on the intro column because the symlinked prod Prisma client's
 * types predate it (regenerated at deploy); the value is present at runtime.
 */
export function planIntroMonthlyCents(plan: { priceCents: number }): number | null {
  const v = (plan as PlanIntroFields).introPriceCents;
  if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(v) || v < 0) return null;
  const cents = Math.round(v);
  if (cents >= plan.priceCents) return null;
  return cents;
}

/**
 * How many of the first term's months are billed at the intro rate. NULL / invalid
 * => the WHOLE first term (returned as null so callers apply it across every month).
 * Clamped to >= 1 so a stray 0 can never zero the intro window. `plan` is `unknown`
 * for the same stale-client reason as above.
 */
export function planIntroTermMonths(plan: unknown): number | null {
  const v = (plan as PlanIntroFields | null | undefined)?.introTermMonths;
  if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(v) || v < 1) return null;
  return Math.round(v);
}

/**
 * Cents knocked off the FIRST term because of the intro rate — 0 when there is no
 * intro. Expressed as a REDUCTION of the regular term total (not a second price)
 * so the regular term price stays the single source of truth and the renewal math
 * is untouched:
 *
 *   discount = (regularMonthly − introMonthly) × introMonths × (1 − termDiscount)
 *
 * `introMonths` is `min(introTermMonths ?? months, months)`, so a 1-month term is
 * fully intro-priced, and a "$3.99 first month" intro on a 12-month first order
 * discounts exactly one month and bills the other eleven at the regular rate.
 * The term discount is applied so the intro months are discounted consistently
 * with the rest of the term the customer chose.
 */

content.text:
Done. v6 "Editorial" is built and on disk.

## Files (all under `/opt/nxeon/app/newwebsitev6/`, nothing outside it)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `layout.tsx` | fonts via `next/font/google`, `robots: { index:false, follow:false }`, `<div className="v6 …">` wrapper |
| `v6.css` | ~1,520 lines, every rule scoped under `.v6` |
| `page.tsx` | Server Component, `force-dynamic`, all data loading + composition |
| `sections.ts` | table of contents (plain module, no `"use client"`) |
| `marks.tsx` | shared SVGs as **individual named exports**, no `"use client"` — deliberately avoids the object-of-components trap |
| `Masthead.tsx` | masthead + running head + mobile contents panel |
| `SideIndex.tsx` | fixed scroll-tracking index |
| `useCurrentSection.ts` | shared rAF scroll probe |
| `PortalPlate.tsx` | Plate 01 with numbered markers + expanding figure key |
| `Catalogue.tsx` | the 42-row picture index with hover-revealed plate |

## Design plan (pass 1)

**Palette** — cool paper, no cream/terracotta anywhere:
`--paper #EFF1F6` (blue-biased off-white) · `--plate #FAFBFD` · `--press #E3E7EF` · `--ink #11151E` (deep blue-black) · `--ink-soft #454F61` · `--violet #4A1FCC` (printerly violet ink) · `--electric #1A52D6` (links) · `--wash #D6E1FF` (highlighter)

**Type** — Bodoni Moda (didone display, never below ~20px) + Libre Franklin (Franklin Gothic revival = real editorial text face) + DM Mono (labels/figures/coordinates). None of Inter/Geist/Space Grotesk, and none of the Archivo / Familjen Grotesk / IBM Plex the sibling concepts used.

**Layout** — a printed monograph: masthead with running head, asymmetric hero (type left, printed colophon strip right), Plate 01 = the portal art at full measure with an annotated figure key, then one **full-bleed dark colour plate** (V Rising key art) against paper, then §I picture index / §II two rooms / §III specification / §IV colophon. Fixed left-gutter index tracks scroll.

## What the self-review changed

1. **Killed every card grid.** Replaced with tables, indices and plates. Radii are 0 everywhere; no shadow except one plate lift.
2. **The hero "stat row" became a colophon** — mono labels above hairlines with Bodoni figures in an uneven strip, not four equal tiles (that row is the single biggest AI-hero tell).
3. **Demoted the accent to ink-and-highlighter.** Violet only for structure (numerals, markers, the one solid CTA), blue only for links, all saturated colour coming from the photographic plates. Stops it reading as "generic purple SaaS".
4. **Dropped Tailwind utilities entirely** — sidesteps the `.v6 .card{position:relative}` vs `lg:absolute` specificity trap by construction.
5. **Ranking → alphabetical index.** `lib/games.ts` says there is no honest popularity signal, so §I prints all 42 families A–Z rather than a fake "most popular" grid.
6. **Replaced one-click *logos* with a typographic index**, with a real `†` footnote for the two `licenseRequired` templates (cPanel, Plesk) — no affiliation implied.
7. Avoided the `globe-network.webp` art: a globe with ten glowing nodes next to "exactly two regions" would be visually dishonest.

## Then screenshot-iterated (Playwright, static preview harness — no Next build)

Headline 90px→78px (the italic tagline was orphaning "online in" onto its own line); genre column `nowrap` + widened (wrapping made every other index row a line taller); region folio numerals lifted out of near-invisibility; the four plate markers re-measured so none sits on text baked into the artwork; image index switched from `columns` to a 3-cell grid so the rules align; **mobile spec table reworked** — the two price columns were pushed off-screen behind a horizontal scroll, so vCPU/Memory/NVMe/Transfer now fold into a sub-line under the plan name and both prices stay visible. Verified no page-level horizontal overflow at 430/700/1024/1600.

## Findings worth your attention

- **`/logo.png` does not work on a light ground** — its "NXEON" lettering is `#e0e0e0` and disappears on paper. I used `/nx-mark.png` (the blue→violet monogram, which reads beautifully on paper) and typeset the wordmark in Libre Franklin. I did not recolour the brand.
- **Live prices moved while I worked.** `Plan.Starter` went 1598 → 1278 and `GamePlan` minimums dropped ~20% between two queries an hour apart. Something is actively rewriting pricing. Nothing is hardcoded; `force-dynamic` reads it per request. The brief's "~$8.99" is `introPriceCents` 888 — shown as the first-term rate with the renewal rate always printed beside it.
- **Region count is derived, not typed.** "Two regions" / "Two rooms" are spelled from `d.regions.length`, so a third enabled node changes the prose instead of making it a lie. Exact node coordinates are rounded to whole degrees (`50° N · 12° E`) so the page doesn't pinpoint a facility town; `Region.ms` is deliberately unused (the catalog file says it must never be presented as customer latency).
- `stationeers` is the one active family with no landing page; those rows fall back to `/game-servers` rather than 404ing.

## Not verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` from `/opt/nxeon` exits 0 with **zero output** (whole checkout clean, v5/v7/v8 included), and `v6.css` parses cleanly through lightningcss. But I did **not** render the real route: port 3000 is the live prod standalone server out of `/opt/nxeon/.next/standalone`, and `next dev` would clobber that `.next`. So the screenshots come from a hand-mirrored static HTML harness (`/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/`, images `f-d*.png` / `f-m*.png` / `spec3-*.png`) that inlines the real `v6.css` and real DB values. **React interactivity is therefore untested** — the hover-swap plate, the expanding figure key, the scroll-tracked index and the mobile contents panel all typecheck and are simple `useState`, but nobody has clicked them. No git commands run, no build, no deploy.
